tldr: Cloudflare shipped account-free Workers deployments on June 21: `wrangler deploy --temporary` spins up a project with no Cloudflare account, live for 60 minutes unless claimed via a follow-up link. The feature was pitched squarely at AI agents that need to deploy code without provisioning credentials first.
whats_new: InfoQ covered the same temporary-account mechanism on July 10, nearly three weeks after launch, still framed around agents deploying Workers immediately with no permanent account.
why_it_matters: Removes a real integration blocker for agent-built deploy tooling: no Cloudflare account or API token has to be provisioned ahead of time, and unclaimed test deployments expire after 60 minutes instead of leaking throwaway infrastructure.

status.detail: The temporary-account deploy path is live and unchanged since launch; the only development is broader coverage, not a product change.

beats.headline: Cloudflare ships temporary, account-free Workers deployments for agents
beats.summary: `wrangler deploy --temporary` runs any Workers project for 60 minutes with no Cloudflare account required; a claim link makes it permanent if wanted.

beats.headline: InfoQ covers the same feature three weeks later, framed around autonomous agents
beats.summary: Trade press catches up to the same ephemeral-account mechanism, still pitched as unblocking agents that need to deploy without pre-provisioned credentials.

open_questions: Does Cloudflare plan to make the 60-minute expiry window configurable?
Will other cloud or edge providers ship an equivalent zero-account deploy path for agents?
take_for_builders: If an agent workflow needs throwaway Workers deployments (demos, one-off test apps), use `wrangler deploy --temporary` instead of provisioning a service account up front — claim the deployment within 60 minutes if you want to keep it.
